title: Mycobacterium abscesses infection after TMJ arthroscopy
html: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) arthroscopy is widely regarded as a safe, minimally invasive intervention for temporomandibular disorders, with postoperative infections rarely reported. This article presents the first known instance of bilateral superficial cutaneous infection and mandibular osteomyelitis caused by Mycobacterium abscessus subsp. massiliense after bilateral level II TMJ arthroscopy. This 26-year-old female presented with progressive bilateral pre-auricular swelling, pain, and superficial microabscess formation six weeks after arthroscopy.
